title: Russian Drone Strike Kills 5 on Passenger Bus Near Nikopol
detail: A Russian drone struck a passenger minibus carrying civilians near Nikopol, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, on the morning of September 16, killing 5 people and injuring at least 7 others. Dnipropetrovsk regional council head Mykola Lukashuk said Russian forces 'cynically struck a passenger bus... which carried people going about their daily business.' The strike was part of a broader wave of Russian attacks that killed at least 9 and injured 36 people across Ukraine over the preceding 24 hours, including 1 killed and 7 injured in Zaporizhzhia (746 strikes on 52 settlements), 1 killed and 7 injured in Kherson Oblast, 2 killed in Sloviansk (Donetsk Oblast), 12 injured in Kharkiv Oblast from guided aerial bombs and drones, and 17 sites damaged across Kyiv Oblast's Bila Tserkva, Boryspil, Brovary, Bucha, and Obukhiv districts. President Zelensky called the string of strikes on civilians an 'atrocity,' saying 'each of these strikes is about the lives of ordinary people who need to be protected by forcing Russia to stop its stupid war.' Human Rights Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets flagged the recurring pattern of Russian strikes on civilian transport.

title: Zelensky: Ukraine Ready for Energy Ceasefire, but Russia Has Not Agreed
detail: President Zelensky said on September 16 that Ukraine is ready for an energy-infrastructure ceasefire with Russia, following a proposal raised by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner during their visit to Kyiv, but that Moscow has not made a reciprocal commitment. Zelensky drew a distinction between the two sides' stakes: 'For Putin, energy is selling oil and gas. For us, energy is having electricity and gas supplies for our people,' adding that a genuine ceasefire would mean 'no strikes of any kind with any type of weapon on energy.' Despite President Trump's earlier claim that both sides had agreed to halt energy strikes, Kremlin-aligned media continued to frame it as a one-way measure requiring only Ukraine to stop long-range strikes, and attacks on energy infrastructure continued on both sides.
